topic.title: Security and Control of Tool-Using Agent Systems
topic.overview: Tool-using agents encounter untrusted documents, external services, and messages from other agents. This topic evaluates prompt injection, malicious tool selection, unintended actions, and deliberate subversion within those workflows. Defenses include monitoring, communication filtering, and designs that preserve boundaries between task instructions and external data.
topic.whyItMatters: Safety of individual text responses does not ensure safety of executed actions. Evaluation must test the system’s authority, information flow, and feedback loops, including ordinary-task failures that occur even without an attacker.
topic.evolution: The cluster begins in 2024 with extensible agent environments, control protocols, and reward-hacking studies. Subsequent work adds realistic vulnerability benchmarks and indirect-injection defenses. Recent representatives examine activation monitoring, unsafe computer use, and failures of embedding-based message screening, emphasizing that malicious and benign text can look similar in representation space.
openQuestions: How can agents maintain useful tool access while enforcing clear trust boundaries?
Which monitoring signals remain reliable after several rounds of adversarial communication?
